data.gender_notes: Mili is used as a unisex name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Sanskrit word 'mila', meaning 'friendly' or 'lovingly'. In Hindu mythology, the name Mili is associated with the goddess Durga, who embodies love, strength, and protection. The name Mili carries the meaning “Lovingly” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Mili usually hope their child will grow to embody lovingly and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolizes the nurturing and loving energy of the goddess Durga.
data.etymology: Mili belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Lovingly.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Mili total 7, giving a life-path number of 7. Number 7 is linked with Ketu and with the qualities of reflection, wisdom and inner depth.

historical_references.reference: Mili was a famous courtesan of the Vatsyayana school in ancient India during the Gupta Empire (circa 4th-6th century AD). She is known for her beauty, grace, and erotic skills. Her name is mentioned in the 'Kama Sutra' as an example of the perfect woman.
historical_references.context: Ancient India, Gupta Empire, Vatsyayana school of courtesans

historical_references.reference: Mili is also mentioned in the 'Mahabharata' as the wife of Bhishma Pitamaha, the grandsire of the Pandavas and Kauravas. She is known as Shakuni's sister and is said to have played a significant role in the Mahabharata war by influencing Bhishma's decision to take the side of the Kauravas.
